beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact thought process repeatedly updates windowed features before decoding.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR separates the dense image field from the compact state that reasons over it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing groups the dense field without dropping tokens. The DQ-CTM thought process runs for shared ticks with the same parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense representation into the super-resolved output.

params.headline: ThinkSR carries dense features through compact thought
params.note: The recurrence stays inside the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines a dense feature field first, then partitions it into windows while preserving every token.
beats.narration: The carrier is made explicit before the compact thought process touches it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the dense feature field. The window operator partitions that field while keeping every token available to the method.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded before it is windowed

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; its 1.129 million parameters are the second largest of the five methods listed.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison does not support calling the method cheap. CATANet is the smallest model in this table. DQ-CTM-SR uses 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN remains larger, while the reported average places DQ-CTM-SR near CNN baselines and behind the strongest lightweight transformer.
